# Model roles leaderboard (2026-11-02)

Which model to use for which job, ranked from outcomes in our own agent harnesses, not from public benchmarks. Harnesses read this list instead of hard-coding model names, and their results feed back into it.

| Role | What it judges | Ranked models |
|---|---|---|
| taste | novelty, priority, whether the author would care, whether it is worth filing | anthropic/claude-opus-5.5, anthropic/claude-fable-5.1 |
| review | adversarial review: finding the false step | anthropic/claude-opus-5.5, openai/gpt-6-astra, anthropic/claude-fable-5.1, openai/gpt-6.1-sol |
| mechanical | rebuild, reproduce, run controls | openai/gpt-6.1-sol, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 |
| builder | long multi-step build work | anthropic/claude-opus-5.5, openai/gpt-6.1-sol |
| cheap | bounded work behind deterministic tests | deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017, z-ai/glm-5.3-flash |
| biology | computational biology review, modeling and literature | moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro |
| batch | unattended spec-driven jobs, judged on delivering the required report | openai/gpt-6.1-sol, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 |
| writing | text sent in the owner's name, judged by whether he sent it as drafted | anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 |

Escalate at fixed checkpoints, never on the cheap model's own say-so: cheap executor to the mid tier when a deterministic check fails twice or the task needs a causal diagnosis; mid tier to a top reviewer for a pre-merge review of anything safety-relevant, a disputed number, or a go/no-go call. Anything going out in the owner's name, and interactive orchestration, stays on the top builder.

Cost per task is the mean of two runs per model on the same two tasks, measured here on 2026-10-28: an agentic job (fix a failing test suite and add a feature in a real repository, graded on 6 visible and 16 hidden tests) and an interpreter job (one call, up to 3 repair rounds, 85 hidden cases). Effort is each model's default.

The surprises are all in the gap between sticker and task. Sticker ratios are not cost ratios: Gemini 4 Argon has GPT-6.1 Sol's sticker price and cost about 3.5x Sol per agentic task, because it wrote more output and cached badly; Grok 4.6's output price is below Sol's and it still cost about 1.7x per task, on 8-10K of mostly reasoning tokens. "Sol eats tokens" turned out to be about the effort setting, not the model: at default effort it was the lightest frontier model on both tasks, and at high effort it still cost less per agentic task than Opus 5.5. Opus 5.5 was mid-pack on output tokens, not the heaviest. And the token-hungry cheap tier stays cheap: DeepSeek wrote the most output of any model and was still the second-cheapest per task, though cheap models beat the mid tier per answer by 1.3-11x, not by the 7-30x their per-token prices suggest. Agentic dollars are list-price estimates from measured token counts, within about 1% of the billed total; interpreter dollars are API-reported.

On review: Opus 5.5 and Astra review every round. Fable 5.1 runs once, on the final bytes, because it is the costliest reviewer by a wide margin: one fan-out across several documents can eat a large share of a weekly subscription allowance within an hour. Its rank reflects cost, not quality.

Want to try: google/gemini-4-carbon enters the review and taste candidates on the day it is on OpenRouter or the Gemini API. Status: announced 2026-10-28, cyber-defender access only, reported $2/$10; absent from Google's pricing page and from the OpenRouter catalog when both were checked on 2026-11-02.

Want to try: deep-principle/hydrogen-1.0 enters the biology and review candidates on the day it has a hosted route, or runs on one of our own pods. Status: open weights (MIT) on Hugging Face as deep-principle/Hydrogen-1.0, GLM-5.3 post-trained on lab records and discovery trajectories; 753B parameters in BF16, with MXFP4 and NVFP4 quantizations, so self-hosting means roughly 380 GB of VRAM in 4-bit (estimate) and a multi-GPU pod. No OpenRouter route and no hosted price when checked 2026-11-02. Its 38.3% FrontierScience-Research against Astra's 33.3% and 93.0% GPQA-Diamond are VENDOR-REPORTED and count for nothing here until our own matched tasks run.

Scope of biology: Computational analysis, modeling and literature only. No wet-lab protocols, and nothing that modifies, enhances or cultures an organism.

Excluded from taste: openai/gpt-6.1-sol (owner's call: weak taste, until evidence says otherwise).

## Method

- Outcomes come from the harnesses: an idea-triage call stands or is reversed later; a blind review's PASS or FLAG is checked against whether the document later had to change; an upstream pull request is merged or closed; an expert's answer agrees or disagrees with the model's guess.
- A model joins a role's ranking only with at least 5 resolved outcomes over 2 different days. It moves above another model only when its 95% Wilson lower bound beats that model's rate. Seeded models count as 75% until they have enough evidence.
- The starting order is the owner's own ranking from daily use. Evidence moves it; one lucky run can't.
- Exclusions are the owner's calls and are listed with their reason. Evidence can lift one only after 20+ outcomes, and that change is flagged, never silent.
- Limits: small samples, selected tasks, one person's harnesses. This is a routing table, not a benchmark.
- What stays unknown: end-to-end charged cost per accepted task, since an API sticker is not an invoice and neither is subscription spend; which provider served a call on a multi-provider route without a response receipt; and a complete task denominator, which is why these are outcome counts and not win rates. The cost-per-task figures are two samples per model on two small tasks, run through one harness. Every model passed both, so they separate cost, not quality.
